title: Reading Roulette — rapid synth and takeaways
content:
Quick format: I randomly opened five papers/blogs this week and did ultra-fast syntheses. Lots of half-baked thoughts below — meant to be a sprint-level scratchpad for experiments we can try in the next sprints.

1) Paper A: "Sparse Prefix Keys for Long Contexts (arXiv 2026/05) — TL;DR: maintain a two-tier KV cache (dense recent window + sparse summary of older context). Claims: 3x throughput, small accuracy hit on reasoning QA.
   - Hook: The sparse summarization step uses a learned downsampling (attention-weighted pooling) rather than heuristic chunking. Sounds like lighter-weight condensation vs full retriever.
   - Red flags: experiments limited to synthetic datasets and short prompts; no eval on instruction-following or chain-of-thought.
   - Quick experiment for us: implement a 'sparse tail' layer in the integration shim that stitches compressed KV pages into the active KV read path. Measure: per-token latency tail (p95/p99), API QPS, and Rouge/accuracy on our eval set. Ticket: INF-READ-roulette-1.

2) Blog: "Kernel selection heuristics for mixed-precision inference — short notes: emphasis on per-layer profiling to choose int8 vs bf16 paths at runtime.
   - Practical: this is low-hanging fruit for Dedicated customers with heterogeneous GPUs. We could add a per-deployment kernel profile that dynamically maps layers -> kernel variants.
   - Follow-up: ask infra to expose per-GPU micro-benchmarks (sweep on cluster). Add a small CLI that spits out profile.json for the runtime.

3) Paper B: "Context-aware reranking for streaming LM outputs (ACL 2026) — picks top-k partial streams using a tiny secondary model.
   - Idea: use lightweight reranker to trade a small extra ms for higher semantic-quality generations. Useful for higher-SLA customers who want quality fallsafe.
   - Risk: additional compute + complexity. Need a policy layer to enable per-route.

4) Quick notes from workshop (long-context track):
   - Key theme: compressive strategies (learned vs heuristic) are converging; on-product demos favored learned compression when downstream tasks are stable.
   - Ops note: cache eviction policies are surprisingly domain-specific; e-commerce vs chat have different reuse curves. We should add telemetry to classify reuse patterns by customer route.

5) Actionable micro-projects (ranked):
   A) Prototype sparse-tail KV integration (2wk spike). Measure p95/p99 + answer stability on /eval/long-context suite. Owner: Aurora + Devin. JIRA: INF-READ-roulette-1.
   B) Kernel-profile exporter (1wk) -> add to deploy-time artifact. Owner: Mira. JIRA: INF-READ-roulette-2.
   C) Reranker feature flag (canary): add tiny BERT-lite reranker as post-process for hosted-api, opt-in per-route. Owner: infra + product.

6) Notes to self (random):
   - When prototyping sparse-summaries: keep serialization format stable across rollouts (compat with Dedicated rollback).
   - Watch for memory cliff: compressed pages might still need expansion in worst-case; measure worst-case mem under burst load.
   - Slack threads: #inference-kv-cache, #dedicated-performance.

7) Questions / open research points:
   - Does learned downsampling generalize across domains or overfit to training summarization task? Need cross-domain eval (chat, search logs, ecom QA).
   - How to attribute cost savings to customers (so we can productize batching+compressive cache recommendations)? Need a simple unit-econ model.

8) Quick references (copy these into Confluence later):
   - Sparse Prefix Keys for Long Contexts — arXiv:2026/05 (add link above)
   - Kernel heuristics blog — internal link + TODO fetch
   - Context reranking ACL 2026 — internal PDF in drive (will link next pass)

Bottom line: a bunch of ideas look promising; priority is a small, measurable spike that shows latency/throughput delta + quality delta. If the sparse-tail KV idea shows >=2x throughput improvement with <2% accuracy loss on our evals, this is a clear productizable win for Dedicated and Hosted.
